title: Email: Office relocation
passage:
To: All Staff
From: Facilities Department
Subject: Office move

As you know, our team will be moving to the fifth floor next month. To ensure a smooth transition, please pack the contents of your desk [1] Friday, May 12. Boxes and labels will be [2] to each department on Monday.

The IT team will disconnect all computers on the evening of the move. [3] Please do not attempt to move any equipment yourself.

We appreciate your [4] during this process. If you have any questions, contact Facilities at extension 2045.
translation:
宛先:全社員/差出人:施設管理部/件名:オフィスの移転

ご存じのとおり、当チームは来月5階へ移転します。移転を円滑に進めるため、5月12日(金)までに机の中身を箱詰めしてください。箱とラベルは月曜日に各部署へ配布されます。

IT チームが移転当日の夜にすべてのコンピューターの接続を外します。機器はチームが新しいオフィスで再設置します。ご自身で機器を移動しないでください。

この作業へのご協力に感謝します。ご質問は施設管理部(内線2045)までお問い合わせください。

choices: by
until
within
since
questions.explanation: 期限(5月12日まで)に完了する動作なので by。until は「〜までずっと(継続)」で、箱詰めを完了させる期限には使わない。

choices: distributing
distributed
distribution
distributor
questions.explanation: Boxes and labels will be ------- で受動態になるので過去分詞 distributed(配布される)。

choices: The new office has a larger kitchen.
The team will then reinstall them in the new office.
Employees may leave work early that day.
The elevator will be repaired next week.
questions.explanation: 直前の「IT チームがコンピューターの接続を外す」と、直後の「自分で機器を動かさないで」をつなぐのは、チームが新オフィスで再設置するという文。他は前後の文脈とつながらない。

choices: complaint
competition
conclusion
cooperation
questions.explanation: We appreciate your cooperation で「ご協力に感謝します」という定型表現。complaint は「苦情」、competition は「競争」、conclusion は「結論」で文脈に合わない。

title: Notice: Library membership renewal
passage:
Riverside Public Library

Membership Renewal Notice

Dear Ms. Alvarez,

Our records show that your library membership will expire on June 30. To continue borrowing books, accessing our online databases, and reserving study rooms, please renew your membership before that date.

Renewals can be completed online at www.riversidelibrary.org/renew or in person at the front desk. Please bring a photo ID and proof of address if you renew in person. The annual fee remains $15 for adults, while seniors and students may renew free of charge.

Members who renew by June 15 will receive a voucher for one free month of our new audiobook streaming service, which launches in July.

Sincerely,
Member Services
translation:
リバーサイド公立図書館
会員更新のお知らせ

アルバレス様

記録によると、お客様の図書館会員資格は6月30日に失効します。本の貸出、オンラインデータベースの利用、自習室の予約を続けるには、期限までに会員資格を更新してください。

更新はウェブサイトまたは窓口で行えます。窓口で更新する場合は、写真付き身分証明書と住所を証明する書類をお持ちください。年会費は大人15ドルで据え置き、高齢者と学生は無料で更新できます。

6月15日までに更新した会員には、7月に開始する新しいオーディオブック配信サービスの1か月無料券を差し上げます。

会員サービス係

questions.question: What is the purpose of the notice?
choices: To announce a change in the annual fee
To remind a member to renew her membership
To advertise a new study room
To request the return of overdue books
questions.explanation: 冒頭で会員資格が6月30日に切れるので更新するよう求めている。年会費は remains $15 で変更なし、自習室の新設や延滞本の返却には触れていない。

questions.question: What is required to renew in person?
choices: A photo ID and proof of address
A library card and a fee receipt
A letter of recommendation
An online confirmation number
questions.explanation: if you renew in person の文に bring a photo ID and proof of address とある。

questions.question: What will members who renew by June 15 receive?
choices: A free month of an audiobook service
A discount on the annual fee
Free access to a study room
An invitation to a library event
questions.explanation: 最終段落に、6月15日までに更新すると新しいオーディオブック配信サービスの1か月無料券がもらえるとある。

title: The Return of Urban Beekeeping
passage:
In recent years, beekeeping has become surprisingly popular in large cities. Rooftop hives can now be found on office buildings, hotels, and even schools. Supporters argue that urban bees benefit from the wide variety of flowers in parks and gardens, and that city honey is often [1] that produced in the countryside, where large farms may grow only a single crop.

However, some scientists have expressed concern about this trend. Honeybees compete with wild bees for the same limited supply of flowers, and [2], a rapid increase in hives could actually harm local biodiversity. Researchers in several European cities have found that areas with many hives tend to have fewer species of wild bees.

As a result, some city governments have begun to regulate the number of hives allowed in each district. Experts suggest that people who want to help pollinators should [3], such as planting native flowers or leaving parts of their gardens uncut.
translation:
近年、大都市で養蜂が驚くほど人気になっている。屋上の巣箱は今やオフィスビル、ホテル、さらには学校にも見られる。支持者たちは、都市のミツバチは公園や庭の多様な花の恩恵を受けており、単一の作物しか育てない大規模農場がある田舎で作られるハチミツよりも、都市のハチミツのほうが多様であることが多いと主張する。

しかし、この傾向に懸念を示す科学者もいる。ミツバチは限られた同じ花をめぐって野生のハチと競合するため、巣箱が急増すると、実際には地域の生物多様性を損なう可能性がある。ヨーロッパのいくつかの都市の研究者は、巣箱の多い地域ほど野生のハチの種類が少ない傾向にあることを発見した。

その結果、各地区で許可される巣箱の数を規制し始めた市当局もある。専門家は、花粉を運ぶ生き物を助けたい人は、在来の花を植えたり庭の一部を刈らずに残したりするなど、別の方法を検討すべきだと提案している。

choices: less healthy than
more expensive than
more varied than
harder to find than
questions.explanation: 直前に「都市のハチは多様な花の恩恵を受ける」、直後に「田舎の大規模農場は単一の作物しか育てない」とあるので、都市のハチミツは more varied than(より多様)が論理的に合う。

choices: in contrast
for instance
in the meantime
as a result
questions.explanation: 「同じ限られた花をめぐって競合する」ことが原因で「巣箱の急増が生物多様性を損なう」という結果につながるので as a result。

choices: keep more hives on their roofs
avoid visiting public parks
consider other approaches
buy honey from the countryside
questions.explanation: 直後の such as 以下(在来種の花を植える、庭を刈らずに残す)は巣箱以外の方法の例なので consider other approaches(別の方法を検討する)。巣箱を増やすのは本文の懸念と矛盾する。

title: The Four-Day Workweek
passage:
For more than a century, the five-day workweek has been the standard in most industrialized countries. Recently, however, a growing number of companies have experimented with a four-day week, in which employees work fewer hours without any reduction in pay. The idea is not simply to give workers more leisure time. Supporters claim that a shorter week can actually increase productivity, because rested employees are more focused and make fewer mistakes. The five-day standard itself was once a reform: in the early twentieth century, factory workers commonly worked six days a week, and the change to five days was resisted by many employers who feared it would ruin their businesses.

One of the largest trials took place in the United Kingdom in 2022, when around 60 companies reduced working hours for six months. At the end of the trial, most of the participating firms reported that revenue had remained stable or even increased, and the number of employees who quit fell significantly. Many workers said that the extra day off allowed them to deal with personal matters, such as medical appointments, that previously caused them to take time off during the week. The organizers of the trial measured not only business results but also the health of employees, asking them to report their levels of fatigue, sleep quality, and anxiety at the beginning and the end of the six months. On most of these measures, the participants reported clear improvements.

Critics, however, point out that the results may not apply to all industries. Companies that provide round-the-clock services, such as hospitals and public transportation, cannot easily reduce staff hours without hiring additional workers, which would raise costs. Others note that the firms that joined the trial did so voluntarily and were therefore likely to be those best suited to the change. Moreover, some employees found that they had to work more intensely during their four days, which led to increased stress. Small businesses with only a few employees also face particular difficulties, since the absence of even one person on a given day can leave important tasks undone. For such companies, some consultants recommend letting employees take different days off rather than closing the entire office on the same day.

Despite these concerns, interest in the idea continues to grow. Some governments are now considering offering financial incentives to companies that adopt shorter working weeks, hoping that the policy could improve public health and reduce unemployment by spreading work among more people. Labor unions in several countries have also begun to include a shorter working week in their negotiations with employers. Still, most economists agree that the change, if it comes, is likely to happen gradually and unevenly, beginning in office-based industries where output is easier to measure than hours worked.
translation:
1世紀以上にわたり、週5日勤務はほとんどの先進国で標準だった。しかし最近、給与を減らさずに労働時間を減らす週4日勤務を試す企業が増えている。その狙いは単に労働者の余暇を増やすことではない。支持者は、休息をとった従業員は集中力が高くミスが少ないため、短い週のほうが実際には生産性が上がると主張する。週5日制という標準自体もかつては改革だった。20世紀初め、工場労働者は週6日働くのが普通で、5日制への移行は、事業が立ち行かなくなると恐れた多くの雇用主に反対された。

最大規模の試験の一つは2022年に英国で行われ、約60社が6か月間労働時間を短縮した。試験終了時、参加企業の多くは収益が安定または増加したと報告し、離職者数も大幅に減った。多くの労働者は、休みが1日増えたことで、以前は平日に休む原因になっていた通院などの私用を済ませられるようになったと述べた。試験の主催者は事業の結果だけでなく従業員の健康も測定し、6か月の開始時と終了時に疲労の度合い、睡眠の質、不安について報告してもらった。こうした項目の大半で、参加者ははっきりとした改善を報告した。

しかし批判者は、この結果がすべての業界に当てはまるとは限らないと指摘する。病院や公共交通のような24時間体制のサービスを提供する組織は、追加の人員を雇わずに勤務時間を減らすことが難しく、コストが上がる。また、試験に参加した企業は自発的に参加しており、そのため変化に最も適した企業だった可能性が高いと指摘する人もいる。さらに、4日間でより集中的に働かなければならず、ストレスが増えたと感じた従業員もいた。従業員が数人しかいない小企業も特有の難しさを抱えている。ある日に1人いないだけでも重要な仕事が手つかずになりかねないからだ。そうした会社には、全員が同じ日に休んで事務所を閉めるのではなく、社員ごとに休む日を変えるよう勧めるコンサルタントもいる。

こうした懸念にもかかわらず、この考えへの関心は高まり続けている。より短い週労働を導入する企業に財政的な優遇措置を検討している政府もあり、この政策が国民の健康を改善し、より多くの人に仕事を分配することで失業を減らすことを期待している。いくつかの国の労働組合も、雇用主との交渉に週労働時間の短縮を含め始めた。それでもほとんどの経済学者は、変化が起こるとしても段階的かつ不均一に進み、労働時間より成果を測りやすい事務系の業種から始まるだろうという点で一致している。

questions.question: According to supporters, why might a four-day week increase productivity?
choices: Companies can hire cheaper workers on the fifth day.
Workers are paid more for each hour they work.
Employees who are well rested concentrate better.
Fewer meetings are held during a shorter week.
questions.explanation: 第1段落最後に rested employees are more focused and make fewer mistakes とある。B はその言い換え。

questions.question: What was one result of the trial in the United Kingdom?
choices: Most companies saw their revenue fall.
Employees spent more time at medical appointments during work.
The trial was extended to all companies in the country.
Fewer employees left their jobs.
questions.explanation: 第2段落に the number of employees who quit fell significantly(離職者が大幅に減った)とある。収益は安定・増加しており A は誤り。

questions.question: Why do some critics doubt the results of the trial?
choices: The companies that took part chose to do so and may have been especially suitable.
The trial lasted for less than one month.
The employees were not told about the purpose of the trial.
Hospitals and transportation companies reported the best results.
questions.explanation: 第3段落に、参加企業は自発的に参加したので変化に最も適した企業だった可能性が高いという指摘がある。B がその言い換え。

questions.question: What do some governments hope a shorter workweek will achieve?
choices: A reduction in the number of public holidays
Better public health and lower unemployment
Higher taxes paid by large companies
An increase in round-the-clock services
questions.explanation: 最終段落に improve public health and reduce unemployment とある。
